# Review

## Outcome

**Approved**

## Evidence

- All shrimp feeding pathway tests pass (8/8 in shrimp_feeding_pathway, 14/14 in tank_core lib including shrimp_feeding_tracks_daily_food_on_routing_mass_basis).
- All validation tests pass (9/9): pre-step invariant guard rejects invalid shrimp_assimilation_efficiency at 0.0, 1.0, and 1.2; rejects zero shrimp_o2_per_mg_c_respired; and confirms state is left untouched after failed step_hours (including a multi-fault partial-clamp test).
- tank_data tests pass (4/4): includes process_preset_rejects_invalid_shrimp_partition_sum and process_preset_rejects_degenerate_shrimp_assimilation_efficiency.
- tank_scenarios tests pass (3/3 integration + process_preset_mapping_carries_shrimp_routing_fields unit test verifies all 5 shrimp routing fields are carried from preset to ProcessParams).
- Budget conservation tests pass: test_closed_system_n_conservation, test_closed_system_c_conservation, closed_system_shrimp_feeding_conserves_nitrogen, closed_system_shrimp_feeding_conserves_carbon (7-day runs with 0.01g tolerance).
- route_consumed_food (shrimp.rs:184-240) partitions consumed N+C into feces (→ fine_detritus_g_total), excreted N (→ TAN), excreted C (→ DOC), respired C (→ DIC + O2 demand), respired N (→ TAN), and retained (→ reserve_g). All five named parameters (assimilation_efficiency, respiration/excretion/growth fractions, o2_per_mg_c_respired) control the routing.
- Mass basis consistency verified: periphyton consumed is converted via algae_detrital_mass_g() to the organic-matter (N+C) basis before recording in daily_food_consumed_g; fine_detritus_g_total is already on the organic-matter basis (feces enter as (N+C)/1000). The shrimp_feeding_tracks_daily_food_on_routing_mass_basis unit test explicitly verifies this.
- enforce_invariants uses a read-only validate_invariants_inner() guard before any clamps, as verified by step_hours_leaves_state_untouched_when_clamps_precede_a_validation_error and step_hours_read_only_validation_does_not_preserve_partial_clamps tests.
- shrimp_assimilation_efficiency validated with check_open_unit_interval (strict 0<ae<1), matching doc comment range 0.4-0.7 and the default_fraction_sums_are_valid test assertion.
- Preset wiring complete: ProcessParamsPreset has all 5 shrimp fields with serde defaults; process_preset_to_params maps them from preset (not ProcessParams::default()); default.toml defines all 5 values.
- Phase-1 simplifications documented: route_consumed_food line 232-234 notes reserve_g will grow without bound pending reserve/condition bead; ProcessParams lines 171-184 document shared food-quality assumption; ROUTING.md lines 59-98 document the full consumer routing contract.
- cargo clippy passes clean on tank_core, tank_data, tank_scenarios.
- The one failing test (filter_enabled_vs_disabled in substrate_filter_integration.rs) is pre-existing and unrelated — last modified during tanksim-6e5.2.2.

## Findings and Gaps

- The failing test filter_enabled_vs_disabled in substrate_filter_integration.rs is a pre-existing issue unrelated to this bead (last touched in tanksim-6e5.2.2). It does not constitute a regression from the shrimp feeding work.
- All five final-review amendments from the prior cycle have been addressed: (1) enforce_invariants now uses read-only validation as pre-step guard with dedicated tests; (2) reserve_g unbounded accumulation is documented in code comment at shrimp.rs:232-234; (3) shrimp_assimilation_efficiency uses check_open_unit_interval rejecting 0.0 and 1.0; (4) mass basis is consistent — periphyton converted to organic-matter basis via algae_detrital_mass_g before recording, and detritus is already on that basis; (5) preset/materialization path carries all shrimp routing fields end-to-end.

## Follow-up and Amendments

None.
